Natural_Language: Acceptance means the act of an authorized representative of the Government by which the Government, for itself or as agent of another, assumes ownership of existing identified supplies tendered or approves specific services rendered as partial or complete performance of the contract.

Validation_Notes: Definitional proposition. Establishes meaning of acceptance for Part 46. Atomic and self-contained.

Natural_Language: Conditional acceptance means acceptance of supplies or services that do not conform to contract quality requirements, or are otherwise incomplete, that the contractor is required to correct or otherwise complete by a specified date.

Validation_Notes: Definition with conditional structure: nonconformance plus correction requirement triggers conditional acceptance classification. HIGH-RISK due to implication. The definition implies that both conditions must be present for conditional acceptance to apply.

Natural_Language: Contract quality requirements means the technical requirements in the contract relating to the quality of the product or service and those contract clauses prescribing inspection, and other quality controls incumbent on the contractor, to assure that the product or service conforms to the contractual requirements.

Validation_Notes: Definition combining two components of contract quality requirements. Both elements constitute the definition.

Natural_Language: Counterfeit item means an unlawful or unauthorized reproduction, substitution, or alteration that has been knowingly mismarked, misidentified, or otherwise misrepresented to be an authentic, unmodified item from the original manufacturer, or a source with the express written authority of the original manufacturer or current design activity, including an authorized aftermarket manufacturer. Unlawful or unauthorized substitution includes used items represented as new, or the false identification of grade, serial number, lot number, date code, or performance characteristics.
Atomic_Propositions: P_46_101_d_1: Item is an unlawful or unauthorized reproduction, substitution, or alteration; P_46_101_d_2: Item has been knowingly mismarked, misidentified, or misrepresented as authentic from original manufacturer or authorized source; P_46_101_d_3: Unlawful substitution includes used items represented as new or false identification of grade, serial number, lot number, date code, or performance characteristics
Validation_Notes: Multi-part definition. Core definition requires both unauthorized nature and knowing misrepresentation. Third atomic elaborates scope of unauthorized substitution.

Natural_Language: Critical item means an item, the failure of which is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe conditions for individuals using, maintaining, or depending upon the item; or is likely to prevent performance of a vital agency mission.

Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition: either hazardous conditions or mission prevention qualifies an item as critical. Either path independently satisfies the definition.

Natural_Language: Critical nonconformance means a nonconformance that is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe conditions for individuals using, maintaining, or depending upon the supplies or services; or is likely to prevent performance of a vital agency mission.
